originalReferencePrompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Asset type: a polished landscape brand identity presentation board for a Korean music software family, brand name "도요" / "doyo". This is an original professional design exploration, not a website screenshot.
Primary request: Visualize an excellent Korean and English typographic logo, a simple bird icon logo and a wide brand banner together in one coherent identity board. Figma is a STRUCTURAL reference only: playful geometric primitives, modular shape language, precise typography, family consistency, quiet professional creative-tool confidence. Do not copy Figma's logo, its signature stacked symbol or its rainbow palette.
Brand: musicians who make, practice, listen and share, with honest creative attempts and their own rhythm. A hint of the gently bobbing woodcock bird meme, but the identity must work as a still graphic. Friendly, witty and grown up, suitable for a serious notation editor and score reader.
Subject: a woodcock/sandpiper-derived bird mark, NOT a goose or duck: compact rounded plump body, tiny head merging into the body with a short neck, unmistakably LONG thin straight bill, short simple legs with a subtle stepping stance. Reduce to 4–6 confident flat geometric shapes and meaningful negative space. Small eye at most, no baby eyes, no smile, no clothes. An apricot wing or small apricot accent may integrate into an ink-green silhouette. Make it a memorable logo, not a detailed zoological illustration, and readable at app-icon size.
Palette: ink green #223C3B, warm cream #FFF6E8, apricot #F5B878; restrained accents sky #B7D0D7 and sage #C1D0B4 only. Flat solid fills. No glossy effects, paper texture, gradients, 3D, shadows or noisy grid wallpaper.
Layout: clean spacious editorial board with carefully aligned panels, generous cream margins. Upper main panel: very large bold Korean "도요", balanced lowercase geometric sans "doyo", and the main bird mark. Side panel: positive and inverse logo lockups in ink/cream and a rounded-square launcher icon. A small restrained palette strip. Lower wide panel: a real usable campaign-banner concept using the same wordmark and 3 rhythmic poses of the SAME bird, with modular rounded shapes implying movement without musical-note symbols. Include two understated product-name samples "도요 Note" and "도요 Studio". Make all elements consistent and art-directed, with excellent whitespace and strong hierarchy.
Text verbatim, only these strings as needed: "도요", "doyo", "도요 Note", "도요 Studio". Correct Korean Hangul is crucial. DOYO spelled D O Y O. No other slogans or filler text, no fake UI, no arbitrary brand names, no watermark.
Wide 3:2 landscape composition, exceptionally crisp vector-like edges and large legible typography.

previousMonochromeStudies.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Asset: refined landscape logo and rhythmic silhouette study for Korean music app family "도요" / "doyo".
Input images 1–3 are MOVEMENT AND POSTURE REFERENCES: the user's woodcock rocking walk. Study the actual long-billed adult bird (not the chicks): compact low horizontal plump body, almost no visible neck, long slim bill pointing gently downward, short legs that alternately compress/bend and extend, making the WHOLE BODY visibly lower and rise. The identity should come from this rhythmic low-to-high SILHOUETTE, not decorated wings or cheerful paint.
Critical user correction: draw every bird as ONE SOLID INK COLOR ONLY. Use cocoa-charcoal #3E332F as the single ink. No colored belly, no different wing color, no plumage patches, no gradients, no internal feathers, no shadows. A tiny negative-space eye may be used. Use leg/body negative space. The silhouette must be very recognizable in monochrome.
Design: cute through proportions and the authentic slightly crouching, bobbing woodcock gait. Not a generic tall standing bird or goose with a lifted marching foot. No long neck, no oversized cartoon feet, no dodo, no smile, no clothes. Keep the same low rounded body, head and beak across poses. Make the difference in BENT LEG ANGLES and resulting body height obvious. The lower/crouched pose has both legs visibly flexed under the body; the extended pose rises with straighter legs while stepping forward. Do not just rotate the entire bird.
Figma is a structural reference only: clear modular forms, balanced negative space, elegant geometric construction, precise typography. No copied Figma mark or rainbow scheme.
Layout: professionally designed spacious 3:2 landscape board on an almost-white neutral background #F6F3ED. Top left is a confident large main logo using one slightly compressed/bobbing bird silhouette with bold clean Korean "도요" and lowercase geometric sans "doyo", matching the original understated strong typographic approach, not bubble font. Top right shows the SAME single-color icon on three restrained background squares: blue-gray #C3CDD5, warm clay #D7B5A3, muted lavender #C9C2D2. These are background color experiments; the bird is the SAME cocoa ink on all three. Do not settle a full palette or add color inside the bird.
Bottom is a large legible four-pose horizontal motion sequence of the SAME adult bird: slightly extended, compressed low, extended high, compressed low again. Same physical body dimensions; a fine common ground guide helps compare body heights, NO ground shadows. The pose changes must be anatomically plausible and convey the user's actual reference gait, not a typical cheerful walking cartoon. Small clean phase labels can be the numerals "01", "02", "03", "04" only.
Include small product-name typography samples "도요 Note" and "도요 Studio" at the bottom edge. Exact text ONLY: "도요", "doyo", "도요 Note", "도요 Studio", "01", "02", "03", "04". No extra captions, note symbols, headphones, beat doodles or watermarks. Crisp flat vector-like graphics. All source photo environment, camera texture and chicks are excluded from the output.

Asset: a genuinely wide horizontal brand banner for "도요" / "doyo", a family of music practice and notation tools. Target wide 3:1 composition.
Input image 1 is the authoritative latest logo and POSE reference. Preserve the cocoa single-ink woodcock silhouette from this reference, including the long downward bill, low plump body with a short neck, tiny negative-space eye, short articulated legs and understated feet. Use exactly the SAME body outline/proportions across all poses.
The important brand gesture is the woodcock rocking walk: legs bend and extend so the body alternately lowers and rises, as in the reference's numbered lower row. This is not a generic raised-foot march. Show three adults as a deliberate motion study across the banner: extended, LOW compressed with clearly bent legs, extended. Same bird at three phases, no chicks.
Every bird is ONE flat cocoa ink #3E332F ONLY. No colored wing, no belly patches, no internal feather decoration, no gradients or shadows. Do not introduce a new bird design.
Typography: on one side leave a strong spacious brand anchor with exactly Korean "도요" and lowercase "doyo", the bold quiet geometric typography from input image 1. No slogan or additional copy. On the other side three same-size woodcock phases with the rhythmic high/low/high body heights and the feet aligned along a common ground. Do not draw a literal ground line.
Background: pale neutral paper #F6F3ED. Only a restrained cropped rounded background form in muted blue-gray #C3CDD5 and another small form in warm clay #D7B5A3 may frame the edges. These background colors are provisional. Keep most of the background open and quiet. No bright yellow, no tomato coral, no old teal palette.
Figma is a STRUCTURAL reference only: modular shapes, confident typography, precise alignment and playful negative space, never its actual logo or palette. Crisp clean flat vector-like graphic art, pleasing adult-friendly wit, not a toy brand. No extra labels, music-note icons, numbers, app UI, badges, watermark, 3D, paper grain or textures. Text verbatim only "도요" and "doyo".

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: Doyo monochrome woodcock brand study board, focused pose correction.
Input image 1 is the edit target. Keep the entire existing board composition, wordmarks 도요 and doyo, product text, background colors, tiny eye, body/head/bill/tail shape and one cocoa ink color unchanged. Change ONLY the legs and feet of the bird silhouettes.
CRITICAL movement correction: all birds face LEFT. The rear/support leg, on the RIGHT side under the belly, must descend STRAIGHT VERTICALLY from the body to a planted small foot. No backward sloping rear leg. The front leg on the LEFT stretches STRAIGHT diagonally FORWARD-LEFT, not sideways, with its small foot slightly LIFTED CLEAR OF THE GROUND. Show a small visible gap under the front toes. It is a subtle reaching step in the woodcock's rhythmic bobbing walk, with weight balanced over the vertical rear leg; no falling backwards, sitting back, split stance, waddling duck, hopping, wide shoes or cartoon high kick. Thin compact feet, no flippers.
Apply this same clear single-support geometry to the main logo and three small icon tiles. In the four numbered gait study birds, maintain their existing alternating body heights but correct the rear support to vertical and make the forward-reaching foot slightly lifted in 01 and 03; 02 and 04 may bring the forward foot close to touching. The front leg should be nearly straight rather than a bent zigzag. Preserve all other design decisions. Render as a clean flat monochrome raster concept with no added annotations.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: supplied Doyo banner. Change ONLY the legs of its three LEFT-facing cocoa woodcock silhouettes. Keep all wordmarks, spacing, body shapes, long bills, tiny eyes, colors, background curves and banner aspect ratio unchanged. The rear leg (image-RIGHT beneath each bird) must be STRAIGHT VERTICAL with a tiny planted foot directly beneath the hip. The front leg (image-LEFT) extends STRAIGHT diagonally FORWARD-LEFT. On the first and third tall bird the front foot is lifted just a little ABOVE ground level, visible gap, while the middle lowered bird has the forward foot nearly touching. Keep the existing tall-low-tall body rhythm. Do not splay the rear leg backwards; no backward lean, seated stance, hopping or cartoon flipper feet. Subtle bobbing-walk forward reach, not a high kick. All birds remain a single cocoa silhouette.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: Doyo monochrome bird brand study, silhouette revision v3.
Input image: edit target board. Change ONLY the upper outline of every bird, specifically the junction of back and back-of-head. Keep the wordmarks, typography, layout, existing monochrome cocoa color, background palette, feet/leg stance, long downward-pointing bill and tiny eye unchanged.
PRIMARY CORRECTION: the current bird has a separate rounded head bump sitting ABOVE a low, sloping back. RAISE AND ROUND THE BACK UP TO THE HEIGHT OF THE BACK OF THE HEAD. The upper back/shoulders must be at crown height, or very slightly higher. Merge the head and elevated upper back into ONE LONG, BROAD CONVEX ARCH, with no neck dip, no separate head bump and no distinct lower shoulder. Think of the huddled, bobbing real woodcock walking with its head tucked low into its raised back: the head is forward-left, back is humped up behind it. The tiny eye and bill root remain low on the front of this continuous compact egg-shaped body. Keep a short tapered tail at image-right, smoothly descending from the high rounded back. Do not simply enlarge the head. Do not create a tall neck, goose silhouette, prominent round head on a lower body, or add wing details.
IMPORTANT retain v2 movement exactly: image-right rear leg is VERTICAL and planted; image-left front leg extends straight forward-left and its foot is subtly raised on the high poses. These legs stay unchanged. Main logo and all three small tiles use the tucked-head, raised-back profile. Four gait poses maintain alternating body heights but all have the continuous head-to-raised-back arch. The rhythm should read through the broad body's lifted hunch as well as its feet. Crisp simple one-ink silhouette, no additional text.
